messages:
IncidentBot: ALERT: runtime-prod-east-1: GPU OOM rate spike detected (pct_errors=28%, window=5m). Severity: P1. Paging oncall.
Maya (oncall): got it, I'm on p1. paging Omar + Priya. tagging runbook: /incidents/runtime-oom
Maya (oncall): quick customer impact check — Zeke can you confirm any active customer tickets tied to this region?
Zeke (support): a few customers reporting 500s for chat completions, one high-volume customer (acme-inc) seeing ~40% failures on some endpoints.
Carla (cust-success): I emailed acme and they confirmed retries happening, they've throttled back but want updates.
Maya (oncall): immediate mitigations: 1) reduce default batch_size for runtime-prod-east-1 to 1, 2) enable KV cache aggressive pruning policy, 3) route 10% traffic to standby region. Omar, can you do 1+2? Priya please coordinate routing/SDR.
Omar (runtime): applying batch_size=1 to pool-rw-01 now. will toggle kvcache eviction threshold to 0.6 -> 0.4. pushing config.
DeployBot: deploy started: runtime-config/evict-0.4 @maya
Omar (runtime): patch applied to pool-rw-01, reducing batching. monitoring token rate and p95 latency.
Priya (sre): setting traffic steering rule: route 10% -> runtime-prod-wus2, will ramp if errors persist. updating opsboard.
Maya (oncall): collecting logs + nvml / allocator stats. Omar, can you paste recent GPU memstats + KV cache metrics (per-gpu) here?
Omar (runtime): past 10m nvml snapshot + kv metrics (trimmed):
```
GPU0: total=48GB used=44.1GB free=3.9GB
GPU1: total=48GB used=45.5GB free=2.5GB
allocator_frag: gpu0=0.28 gpu1=0.31
kv_cache: entries=1.2M hit_rate=0.84 mem_bytes=36GB evict_rate=120/s
batch_queued: avg=6.2 target=8
oom_events: 00:13:51 GPU1 runtime_oom
```
Omar (runtime): noticing allocator_frag >0.3 on GPU1 which is high. eviction isn't aggressive enough given current working set.
Priya (sre): timeline note: first error spike at 2165432053 (root thread ts). mitigation started 2165432108 (batch reduction).
Maya (oncall): hypothesis 1: KV cache plus large batches leads to fragmentation and slow page reclamation -> OOMs under burst loads. hypothesis 2: kernel-level slab growth combined with long-lived attention caches.
Omar (runtime): to test: 1) force kvcache flush on older prefixes, 2) bump eviction concurrency, 3) temporarily drop max_tokens to reduce per-request memory.
Zeke (support): customer impact: acme reported 40% failures, others saw intermittent latency spikes but recovered after retries. they requested ETA for fix.
Carla (cust-success): telling acme: "we have mitigations in flight, reducing batching and pruning cache; next update in 15m." they asked if this is a region-only problem.
Maya (oncall): running targeted kvcache flush for heavy keys now. Omar, snapshot logs for the OOM stacktrace when you have them.
Omar (runtime): paste OOM log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-15T21:35:21Z] runtime: panic: GPU out-of-memory
stack: runtime/alloc.cc:412
kv_cache.cpp:241 evict loop iter 5423 freeable=1.2GB
batcher.cc:97 attempt_batch(size=32) => failed alloc
```
Omar (runtime): note: batcher attempted a size=32 batch even though effective queued avg is lower — looks like one path allowed large batch windows.
Priya (sre): putting a hard cap on batch size in the LB to prevent single-request aggregator from building big batches across tenants.
Maya (oncall): mitigation status: batch cap set -> 4, kvcache eviction threshold lowered, route 10% to wus2. errors dropping from 28% -> 8% over 5m.
Maya (oncall): we should build a post-incident checklist: - full nvml timeline, - per-gpu fragmentation histogram, - allocator slab stats, - kvcache access heatmap, - config paths that allowed large batches.
Omar (runtime): will grab jemalloc/allocator metrics and full nvml trace for the 20m window and share S3 link. also will instrument a metric: max_batch_attempted per minute.
Priya (sre): will open an RFC for safer default batch caps and KV eviction health checks. also propose an automatic fallback to smaller model variant when free memory < X.
Zeke (support): logging customer updates: acme notified, they'll test and revert if they see regressions.
Maya (oncall): final immediate status: P1 -> P2 (impact decreasing), keep follow-ups: Omar to attach logs, Priya to draft runbook improvements, SRE/Runtime postmortem owners: Omar + Priya. assignment noted.
Maya (oncall): handoff: I'm leaving for break, Priya you're on next escalation. Priya acknowledged?
Priya (sre): ack, I'm primary for follow-up. will keep monitoring and start timeline + hypothesis doc.
Omar (runtime): uploading artifacts: nvml_trace_2165432050-2165432170.tar.gz -> s3://rw-internal/incidents/2165432100/nvml.tar.gz
Omar (runtime): also uploading allocator histograms and kvcache heatmap -> s3://rw-internal/incidents/2165432100/artifacts/
Maya (oncall): thanks team. if errors re-spike, re-pager. closing active paging but leaving thread open for RCA coordination.
Carla (cust-success): I'll keep acme updated on RCA ETA. please ping me when we have a root cause.
IncidentBot: Incident P1->P2: automated severity reduction recorded at 2165432175. Metrics link: https://monitoring/runs/2165432100
